theorem example_thm (AB CD EF : Line) (h1 : ¬AB.intersectsLine EF) (h2 : ¬CD.intersectsLine EF) : ¬AB.intersectsLine CD := by
  -- Assume AB and CD are parallel to EF.
  -- We need to show AB is parallel to CD.
  intro h3
  -- If AB and CD are not parallel, they would intersect.
  -- If AB intersects CD, then AB and EF would also intersect, which contradicts h1.
  apply h1
  -- Use the fact that AB and EF are parallel to EF to conclude that AB does not intersect EF.
  apply AB.intersectsLine_trans _ h3
  apply h2
```

theorem if_two_straight_lines_are_parallel_to_a_third_then_they_are_parallel_to_each_other (a b c d₁ d₂ e f : Point) (AB CD EF : Line) (h1 : ¬(AB.intersectsLine EF)) (h2 : ¬(CD.intersectsLine EF)) : ¬(AB.intersectsLine CD) := by
  -- Assume that AB and CD are both parallel to EF.
  -- We need to show that AB and CD do not intersect each other.
  intro h3
  -- If AB and CD were to intersect, then EF would have to intersect one of them as well, contradicting the parallelism.
  have h4 : EF.intersectsLine AB ∨ EF.intersectsLine CD := by
    apply or_iff_not_imp_left.mpr
    intro h5
    -- If EF does not intersect AB, then EF being parallel to AB implies CD intersects EF.
    apply Line.intersectsLine_trans h3 h5
  -- This contradicts the assumption that AB and CD are both parallel to EF.
  cases h4 with
  | inl h4 => contradiction
  | inr h4 => contradiction
```
